title: have to, must, mustn't, don't have to, should
en:
have to — obligation from rules or circumstances: We have to wear a helmet on site. Past: had to. Questions: Do you have to…?

must — strong obligation, often the speaker's own opinion or written rules: I must call my mother. Visitors must sign in.

mustn't — it is forbidden: You mustn't smoke here. don't have to — it is not necessary (but you can): You don't have to come on Saturday.

should / shouldn't — advice, the right thing to do: You should back up your files. You shouldn't work so late.

All of them + infinitive without to (except have to): must go, should go.
ru: have to — обязанность по правилам (прошедшее — had to); must — сильная обязанность, личное мнение, письменные правила; mustn't — нельзя (запрет); don't have to — не обязательно; should — совет. После must / should — глагол без to.

boss.situation: Write instructions for a new colleague: what they must, have to, don't have to and should do in their first week, and one thing they mustn't do.
samples: You have to sign the safety induction on your first day.
You must wear a helmet on the plant site.
You don't have to come to the Monday meeting in your first week.
You mustn't share your password with anyone.
You should read our main procedures before testing controls.

qs.q: You ___ smoke in the office. It's against the rules.
Tomorrow is a holiday, so I ___ go to work.
You look tired. You ___ take a break.
Do you ___ wear a uniform at work?
qs.exp: Question about rules → Do you have to…?

qs.q: Yesterday I ___ stay late to finish the report.
Visitors ___ sign in at reception.
She ___ work on Saturdays — it's in her contract.
You ___ eat so much sugar. It's bad for you.
“You don't have to come” means “You are not allowed to come”.
qs.exp: don't have to = not necessary; mustn't = not allowed.

qs.q: “I must to go” is correct.
qs.exp: must + infinitive without to: I must go.

qs.q: You ___ (not / have to) bring your laptop. We have computers.
a: don't have to
do not have to

qs.q: We ___ (have to) wait an hour for the bus yesterday.
a: had to

qs.q: You ___ touch that cable — it's dangerous!
a: mustn't
must not

qs.q: I think you ___ talk to your manager about it.
a: should

qs.q: ___ he have to work tonight?
a: Does

qs.q: Employees ___ wear a helmet on site. It's the law.
a: must
have to

qs.q: Put the words in the correct order.

qs.a: we had to change the plan

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “You must to sign the form.”
a: You must sign the form.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “She have to work late today.”
a: She has to work late today.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “You mustn't come tomorrow if you don't want. It's optional.”
a: You don't have to come tomorrow if you don't want. It's optional.
You don't have to come tomorrow if you don't want to. It's optional.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “Yesterday I must stay at work until nine.”
a: Yesterday I had to stay at work until nine.

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “Do I must pay now?”
a: Do I have to pay now?
Must I pay now?
qs.exp: Do I have to…? / Must I…?

qs.q: Correct the mistake: “You should to see a doctor.”
a: You should see a doctor.

a: You must wear a helmet on site.
You have to wear a helmet on site.
You must wear a hard hat on site.
You have to wear a hard hat on site.
You must wear a helmet on the site.
You have to wear a helmet on the site.

qs.q: Тебе не обязательно приходить в субботу.
a: You don't have to come on Saturday.
You do not have to come on Saturday.

qs.q: Здесь нельзя курить.
a: You mustn't smoke here.
You must not smoke here.
You can't smoke here.
You cannot smoke here.

a: You should talk to your manager.
You should speak to your manager.
You should talk to the manager.
You should speak to the manager.
You should talk with your manager.

qs.q: Вчера мне пришлось остаться допоздна.
a: Yesterday I had to stay late.
I had to stay late yesterday.
Yesterday I had to stay at work late.

qs.q: Тебе нужно подписывать этот документ?

You should not work so late.

a: Visitors must sign in at reception.
Visitors have to sign in at reception.
